chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman — can one drink from her residue (of water)? He said: Yes, and he cannot perform wudu from it.

key_terms.الحائض: The menstruating woman (ha'id/ha'idha); a woman in the state of hayd (menstruation), which carries specific jurisprudential rulings regarding ritual purity
key_terms.سؤر: Su'r: the residual water or food left after someone has drunk or eaten from a vessel; the leftover, in this context water in which a menstruating woman has drunk
key_terms.يتوضأ: To perform wudu: the ritual ablution required before prayer and other acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Can one drink from the leftover water of a menstruating woman according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la posed a question to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the su'r (residual water) of a menstruating woman, asking whether drinking from it is permissible. The Imam affirmed that drinking is permissible, but ruled that performing wudu from it is not. This ruling distinguishes between two uses of residual water: consumption is permitted while its use for ritual purity is prohibited, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential view that menstruation causes a specific ritual impurity affecting wudu validity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the menstruating woman, ‘Can one drink from her residue (of water)?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, and he cannot perform Ablution (Wudhu) from it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Ftakam from al-Husayn ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Can a woman during her Hayd (menses) drink water which is her own leftover? 5 He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is permissible for her to do so but she must not use it for Wudu 5 .
